title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 18)
summary: Episode 18 of the Meditations reading, starting book 7 in a new recording space. NH discusses the fear of losing past successes, including muscle gains, and why what you achieved once can be achieved again. He also covers escapism as a slavery to pleasure, being fully present, honestly judging your own abilities, accepting help, not fearing the future, and uprightness as a choice that isn't fixed by genetics or environment.
claims: Success makes him anxious that he'll lose it; he fears his muscle gains could go away
If you achieved something once, you can achieve it again; recurring ideas and values come back even if forgotten
Good values come from human nature and logic, so they re-emerge even after civilisations collapse
Chasing pleasure makes you its slave; escapism disconnects you from reality and yourself
People tied to temptations call independent people selfish; a healthy group needs healthy individuals
Your worth is defined by what you pursue, not by birth
Do everything 100%; anything you can't commit to was forced on you or is a lie to yourself, so cut it out
At work, accepting a task and failing is worse than honestly saying you can't do it and handing it to someone better suited
Stoics aren't solitary or proud; accept help, but never ask for help you won't use
If you can handle today's business, you'll handle the future's; anxiety about it is pointless
Being upright is a choice: environment makes it easier or harder but never impossible, so there's no excuse
